data.content_ref: inline:SRC_002's distinguishing evidence fails the problem's requirement because it assumes genuine reliability gain requires ordering and inter-item coherence. Its own countercondition concedes that if the construct is captured by item-level main effects with no inter-item coherence, shuffling shows no reliability drop even when the gain is genuine. This makes the test useless precisely for the checklist archetypes most plausibly associated with trained non-expert success—simple, independently diagnostic yes/no items (e.g., 'Is the estimated cost above $X?', 'Was the permit filed?'). For such checklists, neither genuine reliability nor mere compliance would produce a drop under shuffling, so the manipulation cannot distinguish the two. The 'only unambiguous evidence' claim is therefore overstrong: it is undefined for the narrow-construct, main-effects regime the problem explicitly targets.
